symptom: exec panicked (nil pointer, scriptXPathResolver) on a CREATE WORKFLOW whose user task targets users by an XPath naming a bare member ([Active = true()]) when App Settings > Workflows names a specialization of System.User; check passed, and with System.User as the user entity exec worked.
cause: exec validates a statement with sc == nil. scriptXPathResolver's closure read sc.alteredEntities unguarded; with System.User the System resolver answered first, so only a project user entity reached the closure.
fix: scriptXPathResolver substitutes an empty newScriptContext() for nil, so every caller (retrieve members, widget member refs, grant XPath, workflow targeting) is safe without a script.
insight: check runs with a script context and exec without one, so a nil-context crash is invisible to check and to tests that build a context with newScriptContext(); test validators with sc == nil as well. The trigger was a setting, not the statement, which is why the reporter saw it only on one project.
